about: I Guarantee It shows George Zimmer, the founder of the menswear chain Men's Wearhouse, in a warm close-up from one of his commercials: grey beard, kind crinkled eyes and an easy smile, looking straight at the camera as if speaking to you personally. For years he ended the store's TV ads with the slogan "You're going to like the way you look. I guarantee it." As a meme, the friendly sales pitch gets attached to anything, from reassuring advice to ridiculous promises he could never back up. The joke is his trustworthy face vouching for something absurd, delivered with the confidence of a man who stakes his name on suits.
origin: Zimmer founded Men's Wearhouse in 1973 and appeared in its commercials for decades, closing each spot with the guarantee line. Online, the catchphrase also spawned copypasta stories narrated in his voice.
usage:
The top box is the promise or the setup, and the bottom box is the guarantee: "I guarantee it". The classic pairing is the slogan itself, "you're gonna like the way you look" / "I guarantee it", but the format works for any confident claim.

It lands best when the promise is either oddly specific or obviously untrustworthy: a software estimate, a weather forecast, a team that is going to win the title this year. Keep the top line conversational, like a salesman talking to you directly.
ideas: you're gonna like the way you look
this fix will only take five minutes
you will not regret one more slice
the meeting will end on time
